headline: Bitcoin Bounces as Optimism Returns to Markets After Holiday
author: Emily Nicolle

paragraphs.text: (Bloomberg) -- Bitcoin bounced on Friday as traders geared up for a bumper return to US trading after the US holiday, with technology stocks set to rally when markets open.

The largest cryptocurrency rose as much as 2.3% to top $62,000 before paring gains slightly, changing hands at around $61,400 as of early morning in New York. Other cryptocurrencies also jumped amid thin trading, with overall volumes on crypto exchanges falling around 25% in the last 24 hours, according to CoinGecko data.

"A move above $64,000 would be a serious indication of a shift in market sentiment," said Alex Kuptsikevich, chief market analyst at FxPro. "However, such positivity should be taken with a pinch of salt, as it has yet to be tested for liquidity when traders return next week. A drop to $57,000 would signal a return to the short-term bearish scenario."

US stocks are expected to open higher with futures climbing ahead of the Friday session. Equities in Europe and Asia also rose, as concerns about the artificial intelligence trade bubble bursting appeared to have abated.

Cryptocurrencies have struggled to perform in recent weeks, with Bitcoin on track for its worth monthly performance in more than four years. The token is down roughly 20% in November, weakened by failing investor confidence after a series of major crypto hacks and mounting regulatory uncertainty following the US midterms.

Large Bitcoin holders have seen most of their unrealized profit margins wiped out in the recent rout, inching them closer to ending the year in the red. The average unrealized profit margin for wallets holding between 1,000 and 10,000 Bitcoin is sitting at 5.7% this quarter, CryptoQuant said in a note on Friday — the lowest level of 2026, and a stark fall from a 33.9% margin in late September.

Overall, unrealized gains belonging to addresses holding 1,000 Bitcoin or more are sitting at $23.8 billion, CryptoQuant said, down from $124.7 billion in September and a peak of $294.4 billion in August 2025.
